title: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation Amendment Bill 2006

divisions.question: That the words proposed to be omitted ( **Ms Macklin’s** amendment) stand part of the question.
That the amendment ( **Senator Allison’s** ) be agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Nigel Scullion
speeches.brief: The report of the Employment, Workplace Relations and Education Legislation Committee on the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation Amendment Bill 2006 was presented and ordered to be printed.

speeches.speaker: Santo Santoro
speeches.brief: The bill amends the ANSTO Act to allow the organisation to manage radioactive waste from other Commonwealth agencies, assist in counter-terrorism incidents, and handle waste from overseas reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel, while reaffirming that Lucas Heights will not become a national waste repository.

speeches.speaker: Ursula Stephens
speeches.brief: Labor supported the bill to expand ANSTO's powers to handle, manage and store radioactive materials from terrorist incidents or criminal acts, but condemned the government for imposing a nuclear waste dump on the Northern Territory against its will, breaking a pre-election promise. The senator also argued the bill could be a step toward Australia becoming a global nuclear waste dump, cited 300 interceptions of terrorist nuclear material since 2002, and opposed the government's nuclear power push.

An amendment to the nuclear waste bill sought to condemn the government for imposing a nuclear waste dump on the Northern Territory and breaking a pre-election promise not to locate one there. The amendment also criticised overriding state and territory laws and procedural fairness rights, appointing a hand-picked inquiry into nuclear power while ignoring alternatives, and keeping nuclear siting plans secret.

speeches.speaker: Lyn Allison
speeches.brief: In the debate on the ANSTO Amendment Bill 2006, speakers opposing the bill argued it enables a nuclear waste dump in the Northern Territory despite a broken pre-election promise, expands ANSTO's powers to handle waste from contractors and overseas reprocessing, and should be rejected in favour of above-ground storage and opposition to uranium sales to China and India, while a supporting speaker argued Australia is geologically stable for a repository and that ANSTO needs these powers for safe waste management.

Senator Stephens moved an amendment condemning the government for imposing a nuclear waste dump on the Northern Territory, breaking a pre-election promise not to do so, overriding state and territory laws, removing procedural fairness for challengers, establishing a hand-picked committee on nuclear power while ignoring alternative energy economics, and keeping all plans for nuclear power stations and waste dumps secret.

speeches.speaker: Michael Forshaw
speeches.brief: The bill expands ANSTO's authority to manage radioactive materials and waste from Commonwealth entities, law enforcement, and returned reprocessed spent fuel, with supporters arguing it clarifies safety roles and opponents criticizing the government's waste site selection in the Northern Territory and its push for nuclear power.

speeches.speaker: Lyn Allison
speeches.brief: The speaker moved an amendment to prohibit ANSTO from conditioning, managing or storing high-level radioactive material unless it was generated by the Lucas Heights research laboratories or Australian health or medical facilities. The speaker argued the government was equivocal about storing overseas nuclear waste, cited conflicting statements from Prime Minister Howard and Senator Campbell, and warned that without the amendment Australia could become a global nuclear waste dump, potentially on Aboriginal land.

speeches.speaker: John Hogg
speeches.brief: The speaker argued against Senator Allison's amendment to the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation Amendment Bill 2006, stating it would undermine ANSTO's ability to assist in radiological emergencies and was based on a fanciful premise that the government intended to import high-level radioactive waste. The speaker noted that importing such waste is currently illegal and that the bill only authorises ANSTO to manage waste from its own spent fuel reprocessing, not to import waste.

speeches.speaker: Amanda Vanstone
speeches.brief: An amendment was not passed, and the speaker moved to adopt a committee report, which was agreed to.

acts.title: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation Amendment Act 2006
